title: ECLASS
usedFor: Candidate IRDI for the Repairability submodel's repairabilityScore property (EN 45554 index).
licence: Free to browse; redistribution is a separate, gated question. Confirmed 2026-08-11 from ECLASS's own Terms of Use v4.3 (2022-03-22): searching the current release (Basic or Advanced, any field including Properties) carries no login wall and is explicitly offered free of charge. But §5.2 governs "any duplication, distribution, communication to the public and any dissemination of work results" derived from ECLASS content — citing an IRDI plus its definition in a published, licence-governed crate is exactly that, and needs either a paid licence or the §4.3.1 research/teaching carve-out (granted by ECLASS Head Office on request, not self-service).
source: https://eclass.eu/en/eclass-standard/search-content, https://eclass.eu/en/eclass-standard/prices, and the ECLASS Terms of Use v4.3 PDF — read directly.
finding: **Corrects the prior `nextStep`, which mischaracterised the blocker as cost.** It isn't: ECLASS Advanced-tier *searching* (Classification, Properties, Values, Aspect, Valuelist, Block, Unit) needs no purchase and no account. The actual gate is narrower and different in kind — redistributing whatever IRDI + definition the search turns up requires ECLASS's separate permission under §5.2, regardless of whether the lookup itself cost anything. A live attempt to search "repair" under Properties in Advanced mode confirmed the search form accepts the term and posts correctly, but did not visibly return results in this session — inconclusive on whether that's a tooling limitation or something else, not a paywall or login prompt either way.
nextStep: Two separate, both free: (1) retry the free Properties search in an ordinary browser (not automated) for a repairability-related term to locate the candidate 02- IRDI and read its ECLASS-authored definition; (2) only if a mapping is actually wanted afterward, email `info@eclass.de` invoking the §4.3.1 research/teaching (or open-source) carve-out for written confirmation that citing that one IRDI in an Apache-2.0 crate is permitted. Do not cite an ECLASS identifier in code or docs before that confirmation exists — free browse access is not the same grant as redistribution rights, and this is the same defect class that put a wrong `urn:eclass:` identifier into a published crate once already.
